newsitem.title: USA: Halliburton sees growth in energy services.
newsitem.headline: Halliburton sees growth in energy services.

text.p: Halliburton Co sees growth in its energy development operations, which integrate the company's traditional oilfield services, technology and engineering businesses, Chairman Dick Cheney said on Monday.

The Halliburton Energy Development unit is working three projects currently, including the $1.2 billion Terra Nova project off the eastern coast of Canada, and has been invited to bid on several others, he said.
"We think we will see more of these types of arrangements in the future," Cheney said on the opening day of the annual Howard Weil energy conference here.
In the projects, Halliburton will be putting up capital and manage the fields, leveraging its core oilfield services expertise with its information management and construction operations, he said.
Halliburton executives declined to disclose the company's investment in the projects or its potential returns.

In addition to the Terra Nova project, the company is teamed up with Mobil Corp on its Parks Devonian field in the U.S. Permian Basin. Halliburton will drill 5 horizontal wells this year and plans 15 wells in the field, he said.
